title: The Unholy Consult
author: Bakker, R. Scott
review:
I finished this a year ago and I'm still thinking about the ending. One of my favorite series of all time.

Please write some more books Bakker 🙏

highlights.text: “You’re right, Esmi. I am a monster … The monster this World needs. Our son—” “Shut up! Shut up!” “Our son is a different kind of abomination.”

Everything was as eggshells in the callused grip of Anasûrimbor Kellhus, be it cities or souls or lastborn sons. One need not fathom his designs to understand the mortal consequences of obstructing them.
Wear a thing long enough, and you will think it something earned. Like the name Anasûrimbor.

The Nail of Heaven glared as high on the horizon as he had ever seen, hoisted upon the shoulders of constellations he did not know—alien stars. The night air kissed what injury he had bared, and for a moment, he could almost breathe
And what did lies matter so long as love was real?
“Their words are never soft, Horse-King … only too sharp too feel.”

The Lords of the Ordeal redoubled their thunderous acclaim. Hell itself had cast open its gates before them. Tens of thousands had fallen beneath the Scald of Dagliash. Tens of thousands more languished dying for contamination. Their Holy Aspect-Emperor had abandoned them for no reason … And yet they rejoiced, understanding, at long last, that murder was glory.
Blackness lay in the direction of Dagliash, but for ash and smoke, fires that could not be doused by waters, heavenly or terrestrial.

And so they awoke, frightened by the dark and wanton turbulence kindled in their souls, by the rumours that they were becoming Sranc, and for the first time they realized how very far they had wandered from home.
For this was the great secret of faith, the making near of distant things, the making home in what was vast with cruelty and indifference.
Nothing guarantees judgments made in one age will be applicable in the next, that piety and justice will remain pious and just come what may.
The Horns flashed mercurial on the darkling horizon, the hook upon which all lines converged. Shimmered as an earthbound twin.
“Golgotterath is now our granary!”

Proyas was relatively certain that no soul in history had killed so many as Anasûrimbor Kellhus. The cities razed. The captives massacred. The sons and husbands stolen in the gullet of night. The heretics burned en masse. Every atrocity, no matter how miserable or spectacular, was but a wheel in the greatest argument of all: that the World should be saved … The Holy Thousandfold Thought.
“We shall eat what Hell hath cooked for us!” he screamed. And so led them all into irrevocable damnation.

“Only we Anasûrimbor can see the Apocalypse,” Serwa continued, “so only we Anasûrimbor can see how murder saves, how cruelty shelters, even though it can only appear as evil grasped within a human span. Sacrifices that boggle hearts are paltry to us, simply because we can see the dead stacked about us all, the dead we will become, should we fail to make the proper sacrifices.”
He reeled, only now grasping the absurd consequences of his conversion … How he had fallen in love with his executioner.
“What,” he asked, “do they call women who love fools in your country?” She did not so much as blink. “Wives.”
For no matter how indifferent the Gods, surely sins such as these must arouse them … But nothing happened.
To speak truth to another is to set aside interest and ambition, to either possess faith in another’s estimations or be indifferent to them. The honour of truth is indistinguishable from the horror.
All power shits. All power sleeps. Strength must be aimed, and so are all things exposed, all things weak. To despise weakness is to loathe existence itself

There were a thousand Hells for a hundred Heavens—so many more ways to drown in fire and anguish than to wander meadows in paradise. How? How could anyone be so low, so base, as to willingly sacrifice their very souls to monstrous Eternity? How could anyone embrace wickedness?
Piety was simple, and the World, woefully complex.

“You have been your Enemy! You know Him as even the Gods cannot! Now you, alone of all Men living, know the value of salvation! The beauteous miracle that is honour! The breathtaking gift that is justice! As warriors understand peace, so you understand evil! You know it as you know yourselves, and you hate it as you hate yourselves!”
He realized, even though he lacked the words to voice it, that he stood upon Conditioned Ground. That a place had been prepared.
Scripture, the Great Kyranean once observed, is history inked in madness.
“Accursed—!” he began only to stumble upon the crack in his sacred voice … “Accursed be Nersei Proyas!”
“Lies … For the Dûnyain, these things are naught but tools, two keys to two different arenas of the World. Tell me which is greater: The truth that sees Men extinct, or the lie that sees them saved?”
The kernel of all madness resides in the clarity of its unreason.
To spy your enemy from afar is to spy the very thing he is blind to: his place in the greater scheme. To spy yourself from afar is to live in perpetual fear.
And his phallus hooked high across his strapped abdomen, a bow strung for war … And glory.

She does want to vomit, but for the idea of delivering a newborn soul—her first child!—to such straits, to such an evil time and place! Had any cradle been more ill-omened, more terrifically malformed?
“You believe the one speaking is Kelmomas,” the Holy Aspect-Emperor said, “and that the one whispering is Samarmas, not realizing the two of you continually trade places.”

“I am a tyrant, Akka, the most terrible soul to walk this World in an Age. I have butchered whole nations merely to terrorize their neighbours. I have authored the death of a thousand thousand souls, glutted the Outside with the fat of the living. Never has a mortal been so feared, so hated, so adored as I … “The Hundred themselves raise arms against me!” He actually seemed to swell as he spoke, bloat across dimensions of dark import. “I am the very thing I must be, if this World is to survive.”
“I am your mother. But you-you, Kel, are no one’s child.”

Galeoth thanes, Shigeki surgeons, Ainoni warrior slaves, Nansur columnaries, Khirgwi marauders … it did not matter. For a span of watches, they knew Grace … And in the shadow of Apocalypse, that was gift enough.

A full quarter of their number had been lost at Irsûlor. Another quarter had perished at Dagliash, if not in the Scalding, then in its nightmarish consequence. The vagaries of disease, murder, and attrition had consumed the rest. And yet, fairly one hundred thousand souls assembled across the blasted tracts of Shigogli, half again as many Men as Anasûrimbor Celmomas had mustered in Far Antiquity, and at least three times the number of Cu’jara Cinmoi’s Ishroi.
May your bread, Silence our daily hunger. Judge us not according to our trespasses, But according to our temptations
So did the End of the World begin.

Golgotterath—the subject of so many outraged prayers, sinister tales, and anxious, nocturnal musings. Golgotterath. Min-Uroikas. The Wicked Ark. The greatest evil the World had ever known, bloating by imperceptible degrees, step by dusty step.
They became as gnats. And to a man they thought what every mortal had thought stumping across Shigogli’s bitter plate … No Man belonged in such a place.
“The choice is simple!” he bellowed to the black heights. “Open this gate, live as slaves! Or huddle behind it”—he threw a glance over his shoulder—“and burn! In! Hell!”
Qirri … his cannibal vice. His old, old friend.
“A wife’s curse is as worthless as a sorcerer’s blessing.
“Children often take me for wise. Children and idiots.”

“He is the coal that kindles my wrath,” the Scylvendi retorts, “the knife that compels my will. Do you think I do not see this? Do you think I am numb to his depraved yoke? From the beginning! From the beginning he has ruled my obsession … And knowing this, I have thrown my own number-sticks.

You appeal to reason where there is none! You would put my hatred upon the balance with my desire—show me the mad wages of my design! But my hatred is my desire! My ribs are teeth, my heart a gut without bottom! I am fury incarnate, outrage become stalking sinew and flesh! My shadow cracks the earth, falls upon Hell itself! I smoke for the murder of innocents! And I shall sup upon his humiliation! I shall put out is eyes! Make adornments of his fingers! his manhood and his teeth! I shall hack him into the worm! the worm that is the truth!—truth!—of his nature! For he is naught but a maggot feasting upon carrion and corruption!

“Fear not, Iswazi,” the Holy Aspect-Emperor said—to him. “I am the greater mystery.” Something flashed between the play of pale gleams down the hall, like a cuttlefish in the deep. “I walk Conditioned Ground.” And so was Second Negotiant Malowebi carried reeling into the horror of the Ark.
And now he had returned bearing the death rattle of hundreds in his veins, on his skin, and declaring the People were one. Cnaiür urs Skiötha … The Most Violent of all Men.

The blood of the People was too sacred, he said, to be squandered. He apportioned the widows to the mightiest, enslaved all who were barren. A tempest was upon them, he claimed, and the People would need all her Sons. How the old mothers had crowed. They would weep for the privilege living so long to see his Coming. They would stoop to earth before him, clawing the grasses, baring the soil to his feet, so they might be one, the Steppe and the man they had called Wrencûx … Redeemer. A savage reflection of his sworn foe.
“The Great are always flawed. Always damned … I had assumed the same of you.”
Fall together, land alone. —Ainoni saying
Who were these Men? How had they come to rule—rule!—the Ark? And more horrifying still, why did the Anasûrimbor know them?

“Where you would shut the World against the Outside, and so secure your souls against damnation, I would conquer Hell.” He had broken into the granary of the Living. “Where you would strike the Outside from the hip of the Real, I would enslave it.”
For I have seen the virtuous in Hell and the wicked in Heaven. And I swear to you, brother, the scream you hear in the one and the sigh you hear in the other sound the same.
